definition: The probability that at least one of k sampled solutions is correct (verified by tests or checkers).
details: The probability that at least one of k sampled solutions is correct (verified by tests or checkers). The standard metric for code and any verifiable generation; the gap between pass@1 and pass@k measures how much value verifiers and retries can extract.

explainer.lead: Pass@k is the probability that at least one of k sampled solutions passes the tests or checkers. It is the standard measure for code generation and other verifiable tasks, because the gap between pass@1 and pass@k shows how much retries and verifiers can extract.

tiers.eli5: If you get one guess at a puzzle you often fail, but if you may try five times and any correct attempt counts, your odds of getting it right go up a lot.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers report pass@1 and pass@k side by side to separate model quality from the value of sampling and selecting. A pitfall is comparing pass@k across different k or sampling temperatures, which makes numbers incomparable.
tiers.paperLevel: Pass@k is the probability that at least one of k i.i.d. samples is correct as judged by tests or a checker; it rises with k and depends on the sampling temperature. It measures correctness only against the available verifier, so weak tests inflate it.

explainer.example: Generate 100 candidate programs per problem, count how many pass the unit tests, and compute the fraction of problems where at least one of the first k candidates passes.
